subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards support a documented opt-in append or hybrid payload mode for long replies, or must fixes stay within the full-content CardKit contract?
rationale: The current full-content behavior was intentionally added to prevent truncation, while the newest live repro says cadence-only coalescing did not solve the latency regression; choosing a payload mode is a compatibility and product tradeoff.

options.title: Allow A Proven Opt-In Mode
options.body: Keep full-content as the default, but allow a narrowly documented append or hybrid mode only after live Feishu/Lark proof shows complete final content and improved long-reply timing.

options.title: Stay Full-Content Only
options.body: Reject append-mode config and require any fix to reduce update pressure while preserving the documented full-content CardKit contract.

options.title: Pause For More Evidence
options.body: Keep the issue open but defer implementation until reporters provide redacted gateway/CardKit timing logs from current main or beta.

recommendation.title: Allow A Proven Opt-In Mode
recommendation.body: Keep full-content as the default, but allow a narrowly documented append or hybrid mode only after live Feishu/Lark proof shows complete final content and improved long-reply timing.
